newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU probe of Boeing, McDonnell to start this week.
newsitem.headline: EU probe of Boeing, McDonnell to start this week.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday that the European Commission would start an in-depth probe into the alliance between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas this week, adding that he may have underestimated the problems with the deal.
"There is going to be a fully-fledged investigation," Van Miert told Reuters as he arrived at the European Parliament to speak to a committee on an unrelated subject.
He added: "I have the impression that I had under-rated the problems."

The merger between the two U.S. aircraft makers was submitted to the EU for clearance last month under EU rules which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions in the 15-nation bloc. It is also being investigated by the U.S. authorities.
Boeing has said that it hopes to have cleared all regulatory hurdles by July.
Van Miert declined to detail his competition concerns but vowed to do whatever was needed to ensure fair competition in the aviation market.

He said in reply to a question he was aware of the transatlantic political problems that a tough EU stance on the deal could cause. But this would not prevent the Commission from doing its job, he said.
"It's not because a case may trigger problems with a third country, be it the U.S., that we should refrain from investigating," he said.
He said the Commission was in close contact with the U.S. anti-trust authorities and that it would keep them informed of any problems it detected.
The official announcement of the probe is expected on Wednesday. It could take up to four months.
